items.title: COCONA（XG）、パク・ギュヨンらが来場。「グッチ」2027年春夏コレクション
items.summary: Gucci presented its Spring/Summer 2027 collection "The Store Show" in Milan, with artistic director Demna staging a retail-themed set depicting coexisting personas such as "rebellious aristocrats" and "eccentrics." Japanese ambassador COCONA of XG attended alongside international guests including Park Gyu-young, Cardi B and PP Krit. Primarily celebrity/activation coverage of the show circuit rather than independent critique.

items.title: 「グッチ」新作メンズスニーカーで中国製を明記
items.summary: Gucci's new men's Drip sneaker (820 euros) and leather slip-on (750 euros) from Demna's debut Primavera collection are labeled Made in China, a first for full-price Gucci footwear in decades. Gucci told the trade press Chinese manufacturers had the most suitable technology/capability for the required quality standard, and that Italy remains central to production with no broad offshoring plan; Kering's CEO called it addressing specific technical needs rather than a strategic shift. Frames lingering tension between origin labeling and luxury positioning.

items.title: Has Gucci proved Made in China has a long way to go?
items.summary: Critical trade-press analysis polling fashion-industry professionals on perceptions of Chinese manufacturing quality following Gucci's Made in China Drip sneaker. Frames the launch as having potentially reinforced rather than resolved consumer skepticism about Chinese-made luxury goods, arguing a persistent perception gap remains between improving manufacturing capability and brand-origin prestige that Gucci's own move may have exposed rather than closed.

items.title: 提供一些关于Gucci涨价的新闻报道
items.summary: Weibo/Sina Finance post reports that between September and October 2026 Gucci raised prices roughly 5-8% on classic lines including GG Marmont and Dionysus handbags and some shoe styles globally, justified by the brand as rising material/labor costs and currency effects. Describes a bifurcated consumer response: "buy now before prices rise further" urgency on classics alongside hesitation on non-core items, with secondary-market prices for popular styles also ticking up. Notable as a counter-narrative to the widely covered China price-cut story, suggesting uneven, SKU-specific pricing moves rather than a uniform discount strategy. No engagement counts visible on the fetched page.

items.title: Gucci推出“中国制造”的运动鞋，丑爆了
items.summary: Overseas Chinese community forum thread titled "Gucci's 'Made in China' sneaker is hideous," reacting to the Drip sneaker's origin label and futuristic design. Discussion notes roughly 95% of Gucci's manufacturing has historically been Italy-based, and that breaking with that tradition undercuts the brand's premium positioning even though the shoes remain priced at luxury levels (~800 euros/$1,000). Represents unfiltered overseas-Chinese consumer derision distinct from trade-press framing. Page did not expose reply/view counts via fetch.

items.title: 古驰最近有什么大新闻或变化？
items.summary: Weibo roundup post summarizing recent Gucci developments: Kering's CEO acknowledged Gucci had grown "complacent in China" with poor store placement and dated retail experiences requiring rehabilitation; recaps the 50-year L'Oreal beauty licensing deal (effective 2027) and the new F1 Alpine title sponsorship from 2027; also references Demna's Milan Design Week exhibition "Gucci Memoria" covering 105 years of house history. Mixed tone combining candid admission of past missteps with forward-looking brand initiatives. No engagement counts visible on the fetched page.

items.title: 구찌지갑 짭인지 분간좀..
items.summary: Korean luxury-goods community gallery thread where a user asks fellow members to help authenticate a Gucci wallet, suspecting it may be counterfeit. Reflects everyday consumer uncertainty/trust concerns around Gucci product authenticity circulating in Korean secondhand/resale discussion, a recurring theme in the community distinct from brand-driven coverage. Specific like/comment counts not exposed via fetch.

items.title: 중고시장 뜨는데 중고 명품은 외면…신뢰 잃은 '럭셔리 리셀'의 추락
items.summary: Korean trade/consumer feature on the collapse of trust in the luxury resale market even as general secondhand commerce grows; cites overpricing, counterfeit concerns and eroding brand confidence as drivers. Notes a broader global pattern of falling resale values for marquee luxury items (Hermes Birkin, Rolex) as post-pandemic savings dry up and higher interest rates reduce the incentive to hold luxury goods as investments. Gucci is cited among the major brands implicated in this resale-market downturn, giving a critical secondhand-market angle distinct from new-product coverage.
